## Highlights

- **Saving works again in release packages.** New saves no longer fail validation because the release was incorrectly identified as build 1.
- **Release downloads are checked end to end.** Archives must decompress completely, and uploaded file sizes and SHA-256 digests must match the validated originals before a new release is published.
- **Compiled maps carry the correct geometry checksum.** A newly generated `.proc` is no longer immediately reported as out of date.

## Upgrade Notes

- Replace the complete package, keeping the engine, renderer modules, game modules, and bundled data together. Retail Quake 4 assets are still required.
- Failed save attempts in 0.13.0 did not produce a usable new save. This patch does not recover those attempts or add compatibility with unsupported older saves stamped as build 1; keep backups and use the version that wrote an older campaign save when necessary.
- Map authors: openQ4 rebuilds render geometry and collision, but does not yet include the Quake 4 AAS compiler. Rebuild navigation with the Quake 4 SDK tools after changing map geometry. The compiler now reports this limitation explicitly; remaining navigation work is tracked in [#158](https://github.com/themuffinator/openQ4/issues/158).
- The experimental macOS packages target Apple Silicon/arm64. Intel Mac packages are not published, and Rosetta is not a supported substitute. Linux ARM64 remains a preview.
- The `macos_graphics_bridge=metal` package is a Metal bridge around the OpenGL renderer, not a native Metal renderer; `platform_backend=native` is comparison-only diagnostic infrastructure, not a release backend. Existing macOS visual-parity limitations remain tracked in [issue #98](https://github.com/themuffinator/openQ4/issues/98), and support promotion remains gated by `docs/dev/macos-signoff-evidence.md`.

## Change Log

- Corrected release build numbering and rejected stable builds made without complete Git history, preventing freshly written saves from being mistaken for unsupported development saves ([#159](https://github.com/themuffinator/openQ4/issues/159)).
- Added full archive integrity checks and verification of the exact bytes stored by GitHub; new releases stay in draft until those checks pass ([#160](https://github.com/themuffinator/openQ4/issues/160)).
- Replaced the map compiler's placeholder checksum with the compiled map's geometry checksum, and added a clear warning when navigation cannot be rebuilt ([#158](https://github.com/themuffinator/openQ4/issues/158)).

## Linux ARM64 Support

Linux ARM64 preview artifacts enabled. First-class publication remains gated on accepted real-hardware native-Wayland SP/MP, dedicated-server, audio, input, display, and package evidence.

| Field | Value |

## Highlights

- **Multiplayer matches are easier to organize, follow and replay.** Managed series support map vetoes, selected-map handoffs, persistent results and recovery between maps. Spectators can switch player cameras from Match Control, replays preserve their selected player, and the configurable chat panel retains conversations and channel drafts.
- **High-refresh gameplay is much smoother while game logic stays at its original rate.** The camera, first-person weapon, skeletal animation, projectiles, moving world objects, lights, and effects can now present an interpolated pose between authoritative game ticks. Zoom markings and joint-bound effects follow the pose actually shown.
- **Experimental rendering has a broader, safer foundation.** OpenGL and Vulkan now share sealed contracts for classic materials, GUIs, interactions, fog, subviews, deforms, and post effects. Optional temporal AA/upscaling, dynamic resolution, GPU skinning, PBR materials, reflections, volumetrics, and indirect-light previews remain default-off and retain complete fallback paths.
- **Vulkan shadows are more complete and easier to diagnose.** Shadow-mapped lights can replace eligible stencil work, combine cached static and dynamic casters, reuse fitted cascades, expose receiver/debug views, and report non-blocking GPU timings without losing direct lighting when a shadow allocation fails.
- **Complex levels load and settle faster.** The `airdefense1` opening avoids presentation work for cinematic frames that are never displayed and skips bake-only light-grid setup during ordinary play. A guarded repeat-load cache can be enabled for evaluation, while the classic source path remains the default.
- **Saving and restoring fail safely.** Unset or invalid GUI animation values can no longer abort an otherwise valid save, malformed GUI and auxiliary data is rejected before partial state reaches the renderer, and incompatible old saves are refused before the active level is unloaded.
- **Internet multiplayer is safer and easier to enter.** Network parsers now reject truncated state at explicit boundaries, remote administration avoids plaintext passwords by default, pure play keeps asset checks without accepting executable code from servers, and connecting opens a compact Quake 4-styled join card over the live map.
- **Liquids and effects feel more complete.** Projectiles and hitscan shots cross liquid surfaces with matching splashes, sounds, and underwater trails; water jumping is reliable; slime, lava, and drowning have distinct feedback; and soft particles now reduce hard intersections between smoke and solid geometry.
- **Everyday controls and presentation received focused polish.** Controller menu traversal no longer fights stale mouse focus, scalable menu text selects a sharper source atlas on modern displays, material texture filtering is configurable again, and light-grid preloading is available in Display settings.
- **Platform and tool reliability improved.** macOS packages bundle OpenAL Soft to prevent long-session audio exhaustion, Linux accepts legitimate repeated-dot save paths, staged packages reject case-colliding files, and `dmap` once again compiles `func_group` geometry correctly.

## Upgrade Notes

- Replace the complete openQ4 package for your platform. Keep the engine, renderer modules, `game_sp`, `game_mp`, and bundled `baseoq4` data from the same 0.13.0 package.
- Retail Quake 4 assets are still required. Point openQ4 at a complete installation, including the unsuffixed language archive such as `zpak_english.pk4`.
- Existing settings remain valid. Soft particles now default to on for new configurations; an existing archived `r_softParticles` value is preserved.
- OpenGL remains the default and recommended renderer. Vulkan remains experimental and opt-in with `r_renderApi vulkan`, applied after restart.
- Temporal AA, dynamic resolution, GPU skinning, modern shared-renderer domains, PBR lighting, screen-space effects, and repeat-load caching remain experimental and default-off. `r_rendererModernQuality 0` and `com_levelLoadModernization 0` retain the established rendering and loading paths.
- Saves from unsupported older development formats are rejected before unloading the current map. Finish an affected campaign using the build that wrote it, and keep backups of important saves before upgrading.
- macOS users should replace the complete package to receive the bundled OpenAL Soft runtime. Linux ARM64 downloads remain preview packages. The experimental macOS packages target Apple Silicon/arm64 and may be unsigned when Apple signing and notarization credentials are unavailable. Intel Mac packages are not published or supported, and Rosetta is not a supported substitute.
- On macOS, OpenGL remains the recommended renderer; the Vulkan option runs through MoltenVK, a Vulkan-on-Metal translation layer. The `macos_graphics_bridge=metal` package is a Metal bridge around the OpenGL renderer, not a native Metal renderer, while `platform_backend=native` is comparison-only diagnostic infrastructure, not a release backend. Visual parity remains tracked by [issue #98](https://github.com/themuffinator/openQ4/issues/98), and support promotion remains gated by `docs/dev/macos-signoff-evidence.md`.
- Server operators should review the updated remote-console, pure-server, package-download, and malformed-packet behavior before replacing a public server.
- Update multiplayer clients and servers to the same build, and finish active managed series before upgrading; structured match views now use schema 4 for persistent results, and spectator-follow requests, player requirements, Duel contender seats, round resets and One Flag map support have changed. Replay older development multiplayer demos with the build that recorded them.

## Change Log

- Added a configurable multiplayer chat panel with wrapped message history, preserved scroll position, per-channel draft and sent-message recall, and adjustable size, placement, opacity and fade timing.
- Fixed multiplayer warmup with bots: bots fill player slots without voting for unready humans, Duel waits for its seated contenders, and players can cancel countdown by withdrawing readiness.
- Restored automatic starts when casual ready-up is disabled, kept bots out of option-vote majorities, and preserved the ongoing match state on remote clients between rounds.
- One Flag and Arena One Flag can now complete captures on original CTF maps: missing neutral flags use stock assets at a central pickup location, while authored objectives take precedence. Remote clients also receive server announcer cues correctly.
- Freeze Tag rescues now work when a teammate reaches a frozen player, and overkills no longer destroy the body needed for the rescue.
- DeadZone scores only eligible controllers during live play, handles lost tokens and contested zones consistently, and supports map-authored zones that do not require a token.
- Managed Red Rover converts defeated players without opening voluntary live team changes, preserves declared rosters and restores their home sides between rounds.
- Managed listen servers honor initial auto-join, and authorized force-ready actions now complete their countdown and enter gameplay.
- Remote players now keep their accepted join choice, and managed team or roster changes update their own client correctly.
- Managed series now load the selected map after veto and publish the final series result after review, with matching match reports and committed demo links. Clients can recover from long countdown-to-play world resets without being disconnected for predicting ahead.
- Managed Duel admits its two contestants reliably and gives each their own timeout budget, with matching request and resume controls.
- Managed summaries now distinguish the committed winner, forfeit, draw and abort from the original scores. Winning identities and names survive later player changes, and Match Control shows Last Result through review and the next warmup until the next countdown or session, even with optional evidence recording disabled.
- Long winner names and forfeit messages fit the result banner, and older chat lines no longer leave distorted text above the summary's chat history.
- Captain invitations are revoked when the captain loses authority, and roster actions explain when they must wait for warmup. Canceled, expired or unsuccessful proposals release their voting slot for the next proposal while retaining normal cooldowns.
- Series check that the selected map file is available before starting the handoff, keeping a missing-map attempt ready for retry. Repeated checks of loose map files no longer accumulate open file handles.
- Added Previous, Next and Free Camera buttons to Match Control's Status tab for spectators, alongside live commands `follow next`, `follow prev`, `follow free` and `follow <client-slot>`, with `follownext`, `followprev` and `followfree` aliases. Server camera permissions still apply, stale direct targets are rejected, and existing eligible bot targets remain available.
- Fixed relative includes in root-level map-cycle scripts on Windows and POSIX systems without requiring replacement assets.
- Fixed remote referee sign-in stalling after the server issued its authentication challenge.
- Competitive pauses now keep remote player and weapon animations frozen through network clock corrections, while gameplay timers resume from their saved remaining time.
- Match Control shows readable status summaries, committed rule values and roster choices in both widescreen and 4:3 layouts, using the original Quake 4 interface art.
- A managed series restored after a completed map can now advance from its recovered review. Duel operators can rebind the current contestants and continue with the saved score and reports intact.
- Match replays retain the selected player across round restarts during playback and seeking, and immediately restore their correct view height while paused. Repeated player-camera changes work while paused, and explicitly choosing free camera still takes precedence.
- Corrected score-limit winners and ties, cleared stale timers between matches, and ended abandoned matches when their last active human leaves.
- Corrected tied scoreboard places and result recording, reduced repeated ranking work, and restored Duel's final table with both finalists retained through review and waiting players excluded.
- Reduced memory allocation and copying during in-memory file generation, and prevented corruption when overwriting buffered data or handling oversized reads and writes.
- Made Windows staging retries respect the option to leave running games open when an install encounters a locked file.
- Added presentation-only interpolation for eligible single-player actors, first-person weapons, movers, projectiles, lights, and effects while preserving authoritative simulation, collision, networking, demos, and save behavior.
- Added default-off native-history TAA/TAAU and bounded delayed-GPU-time dynamic resolution on OpenGL and Vulkan, with native-resolution HUD, menu, console, screenshot, and save-preview output.
- Added default-off exact four-weight GPU skinning for supported MD5 and MD5R models, with CPU-owned collision, traces, decals, overlays, and stencil-shadow data.
- Added guarded PBR materials, OpenGL specular probes and clustered decals, plus bounded OpenGL/Vulkan volumetric, SSR, and SSGI preview paths.
- Added shared, atomic renderer contracts for eligible GUI, in-world GUI, world ambient, interaction, fog/blend, cinematic/post, special-frame, subview, and material-deform work.
- Expanded Vulkan shadow-map ownership, static/dynamic caster composition, fitted cascade caching, receiver diagnostics, debug overlays, and timestamp-query timing.
- Improved shadow-map caster coverage and contact quality for open, thin, and sealed stock geometry while preserving stencil fallback ownership.
- Fixed stale door shadows, false point-light occlusion, unnecessary cache redraws, and Vulkan shadow-diagnostic crashes; cutout casters can update over cached opaque projected shadows.
- Prevented lit decals and other translucent materials marked `noShadows` from casting unintended solid shadows, while preserving eligible translucent casters and `forceShadows` overrides.
- Added backend-neutral whole-frame CPU/GPU measurement and replayable per-map renderer budget contracts.
- Reduced `airdefense1` cinematic and light-grid startup work, and added a guarded exact-source repeat-load cache backed by bounded background jobs and transactional model/world/collision data.
- Fixed animated-model traces so stable surface IDs, reordered snapshots, omitted meshes, and generated backfaces resolve to the correct MD5/MD5R joint instead of terminating the level.
- Prevented non-finite or uninitialized cosmetic GUI values from aborting saves, and strengthened preflight checks for incompatible, truncated, or corrupt save data.
- Hardened Base64, lexer, GUI timeline/restore, render-demo, decal, CVar dictionary, user-command, snapshot, projectile, and hit-scan decoding against malformed input.
- Restored pure multiplayer asset enforcement without allowing package negotiation to install or launch executable code, and replaced plaintext-by-default remote-console authentication with bounded `rcon2`.
- Added the compact multiplayer join card, restored the stock F1/F2/F3/F6/F7 match actions, improved snapshot/effect rate handling, and prevented clients from authoring the clock used for lag-compensated hit judgment.
- Added complete liquid crossing, underwater trail, water-jump, sound, obituary, and developer-lab behavior using bundled openQ4 content and stock media.
- Enabled soft particles by default while excluding depth-hacked and unsupported effects from the fade.
- Restored all six Quake 4 material texture-filter modes on OpenGL and Vulkan with immediate sampler refresh.
- Improved controller menu focus, high-resolution font-atlas selection, machinegun zoom alignment, single-player pause-menu responsiveness, and the Display setting for optional light-grid preloading.
- Bundled checksum-pinned OpenAL Soft in macOS packages and made backend allocation/upload exhaustion fail gracefully.
- Fixed the manual macOS release audit so the exact bundled OpenAL Soft `@rpath` dependency is accepted only after its architecture, dependencies, signature, and install name pass validation.
- Fixed publication of previously staged draft releases so validated downloads can go live and trigger their Discord announcement.
- Prevented legacy OpenGL contexts from attempting unsupported SMAA shaders, texture swizzles, multisample textures, direct texture binding and GPU timestamp queries, retaining the available rendering paths.
- Made renderer self-tests safer on macOS and explicit about optional features unavailable on the current OpenGL context.
- Fixed SDL swap-interval updates after temporary context detachment, Linux save paths containing legitimate repeated dots, and case-insensitive package path collisions.
- Restored `dmap` handling of `func_group` geometry, initialized geometry-tool surface allocation, and accepted generated AAS 1.08 face settings.
- Added contributing and community-conduct documentation and packaged the relevant project guidance with releases.

## Linux ARM64 Support

Linux ARM64 preview artifacts enabled. First-class publication remains gated on accepted real-hardware native-Wayland SP/MP, dedicated-server, audio, input, display, and package evidence.

## Highlights

- **High-refresh gameplay looks smoother without changing game logic.** Players, weapons, projectiles, lights, client effects, and moving-world attachments now sample a presentation transform between authoritative game ticks. View-model effects stay anchored to the pose actually drawn, including the lightning gun beam, while simulation, networking, collision, demos, and savegames retain their original timing.
- **Polish and Russian are now built in.** Text rendering works by Unicode code point, the Polish tables use the correct Central European encoding path, and generated font data is checksum-validated so translated menus and HUD text remain reproducible across packages.
- **The marine hovertank has its vehicle audio back.** Single-player once again creates and updates the engine and hover-pad loops used throughout the vehicle sequence, with safe cleanup during map or engine shutdown.
- **Arena Campaign scoring starts reliably.** Disabling ready-up now also clears the ready threshold, preventing deathmatch-backed Arena cards from remaining forever in a non-scoring warmup.
- **Multiplayer setup is easier to control.** The server menu exposes guarded bot controls, and competitive free-for-all disclosure now accepts the active recipients intended by the match policy.
- **Developer map compilation is more reliable.** `dmap` and other engine-side geometry tools initialize their triangle-surface allocator before generating light volumes, fixing the Windows crash seen while compiling `game/airdefense1`.

## Upgrade Notes

- Replace the complete openQ4 package for your platform so the engine, renderer modules, `game_sp`, `game_mp`, and bundled openQ4 data all come from 0.12.0. Do not mix modules from older releases.
- Existing settings and compatible saves do not need to be reset. As a precaution, retain a copy of important saves before replacing an older installation.
- Retail Quake 4 assets are still required. Point openQ4 at a complete retail installation, including the unsuffixed base dialogue archive such as `zpak_english.pk4`.
- OpenGL remains the default and recommended renderer. Vulkan is experimental and opt-in with `r_renderApi vulkan`, applied after an engine restart. The modern OpenGL visible path also remains guarded and experimental.
- Linux ARM64 downloads remain preview packages. The experimental macOS packages target Apple Silicon/arm64 and may be unsigned when Apple signing and notarization credentials are unavailable. Intel Mac packages are not published or supported, and Rosetta is not a supported substitute. OpenGL remains the recommended renderer; the Vulkan option runs through MoltenVK, a Vulkan-on-Metal translation layer. The `macos_graphics_bridge=metal` package is a Metal bridge around the OpenGL renderer, not a native Metal renderer, while `platform_backend=native` is comparison-only diagnostic infrastructure, not a release backend. Visual parity remains tracked by issue #98, and support promotion remains gated by `docs/dev/macos-signoff-evidence.md`.

## Change Log

- Added presentation-only interpolation for high-refresh rendering of actors, movers, first-person weapons, projectiles, lights, and client effects while preserving authoritative tick behavior.
- Kept view-model client entities and the lightning gun beam attached to the exact rendered weapon pose.
- Fixed weapon swaps that could inherit firing state or leave stale effects behind.
- Added complete Polish and Russian UI tables, Unicode code-point drawing, CP1250 conversion support, and stricter generated-font checksum validation.
- Restored the marine hovertank engine and hover-pad loops with null-safe sound-emitter teardown.
- Prevented partial attachment restoration from tearing down incompletely restored entities twice.
- Restored Arena Campaign countdown and scoring progression when ready-up is disabled.
- Added multiplayer bot controls and validation to the server setup menu.
- Allowed the intended active free-for-all recipients through competitive match disclosure policy.
- Corrected `s_muteUnfocused` transitions so returning to the game cannot leave audio muted for the rest of the level.
- Initialized engine-side triangle-surface allocators for `dmap` and related geometry tools.
- Strengthened the experimental modern OpenGL lighting path with per-light image ownership and missing-binding fallbacks.

## Linux ARM64 Support

Linux ARM64 preview artifacts enabled. First-class publication remains gated on accepted real-hardware native-Wayland SP/MP, dedicated-server, audio, input, display, and package evidence.

- **Windows gameplay is more reliable during streaming and avatar-overlay use.** AMD OpenGL systems now avoid the persistent-mapped upload and fence path associated with driver timeouts under capture workloads, while retaining the modern renderer through a safer orphaned map-range stream. Crash logs also identify the module and relative offset responsible for an exception, making driver and capture-hook faults much easier to distinguish from openQ4 faults.
- **Story checkpoints no longer fail on transient stock-map references.** Save serialization once again treats an out-of-graph area-location reference as null, matching retail Quake 4 behavior, and failed save attempts cannot resume serialization after map teardown.
- **Underwater play looks and feels substantially better.** OpenGL adds depth-aware absorption, scattering, refraction, caustics, bloom, marine snow, and underwater projectile bubbles before the HUD. Swimming speed and vertical control, water friction, and sound occlusion across liquid surfaces have also been corrected. Vulkan retains its existing compatible water tint while broader renderer parity continues.
- **Every retail and Raven map-pack loading screen is now complete.** All 56 base-game and 7 map-pack load images have validated center, left, right, top, and bottom views. Generated widescreen and ultrawide screens are published atomically, so an interrupted write can no longer replace the live image with a truncated file that aborts map loading.
- **Windows respects redirected per-user folders.** The save root now comes from the Windows Known Folder service, so redirected Local AppData and Saved Games locations work without relying on environment-variable guesses.
- **Incomplete retail-asset installs are easier to diagnose.** Startup warns when the unsuffixed `zpak_<language>.pk4` dialogue archive is absent instead of allowing numbered language patches to hide the missing base media.
- **Experimental Apple Silicon macOS packages are more robust.** MoltenVK discovery now supports both loose-package layouts used by openQ4, universal2 candidate assembly and launch validation are stricter, and OpenAL Soft migration builds fail clearly when Homebrew's package is not visible through pkg-config. macOS support remains experimental while visual parity issue #98 and real-hardware signoff remain open.

## Upgrade Notes

- Replace the complete openQ4 package for your platform so the engine, renderer modules, `game_sp`, `game_mp`, and bundled openQ4 data all come from 0.11.0. Do not mix modules from older releases.
- Existing settings and compatible saves do not need to be reset. As a precaution, retain a copy of important saves before replacing an older installation.
- Retail Quake 4 assets are still required. If dialogue is missing, install the base language archive—such as `zpak_english.pk4`—or point openQ4 at a complete retail installation; numbered `_01` through `_04` patch archives are not substitutes for that file.
- OpenGL remains the default and recommended renderer. Vulkan is experimental and opt-in with `r_renderApi vulkan`, applied after an engine restart.
- Linux ARM64 downloads remain preview packages. The experimental macOS packages target Apple Silicon/arm64 and may be unsigned when Apple signing and notarization credentials are unavailable. Intel Mac packages are not published or supported, and Rosetta is not a supported substitute. OpenGL remains the recommended renderer; the Vulkan option runs through MoltenVK, a Vulkan-on-Metal translation layer. The `macos_graphics_bridge=metal` package is a Metal bridge around the OpenGL renderer, not a native Metal renderer, while `platform_backend=native` is comparison-only diagnostic infrastructure, not a release backend. Visual parity remains tracked by issue #98, and support promotion remains gated by `docs/dev/macos-signoff-evidence.md`.

## Change Log

- Added a capture-safe Windows AMD OpenGL upload policy and richer crash-module diagnostics.
- Restored retail-compatible handling of transient savegame references and made save-writer cleanup safe on both success and failure paths.
- Added the OpenGL underwater view treatment and corrected swimming, liquid friction, underwater effects, and sound propagation.
- Capped loading-screen redraw pacing at 60 Hz, accounted for redraw cost, and reduced unnecessary progress updates during large reads.
- Completed and validated the five-view levelshot inventory for every supported retail and Raven map-pack load image.
- Made generated widescreen loading-screen publication atomic, collision-resistant across concurrent processes, and safely fall back to the original image on failure.
- Added a specific warning for missing base dialogue archives in partial Quake 4 installations.
- Switched Windows save-root discovery to the system Known Folder service with hardened fallbacks and consistent native path display.
- Improved reliable-network overflow handling, snapshot initialization, client visibility packing, large-allocation safety, and presentation throttling.
- Corrected localized menu-header capitalization and added missing match-series and vote-cooldown translations.
- Hardened experimental macOS MoltenVK staging, provenance, universal2 assembly, signing, package documentation, and Finder-style launch validation.
- Made the optional macOS OpenAL Soft provider use an explicit pkg-config lookup with clearer Homebrew setup guidance.
- Kept sanitizer builds linkable across the in-process BSE and runtime renderer boundary, and closed MD5R export files through the engine-owned filesystem API.
- Strengthened release artifact validation and reproducible GameLib staging across supported build hosts.

## Linux ARM64 Support

Linux ARM64 preview artifacts enabled. First-class publication remains gated on accepted real-hardware native-Wayland SP/MP, dedicated-server, audio, input, display, and package evidence.
